PENN Entertainment Posts Record Retail Revenue and a 45% Adjusted EBITDA Jump in Q3 2026

Published November 6, 2026 · 3 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

PENN Entertainment reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $1.84 billion, up 7.1% from the same period a year earlier, alongside a company-wide adjusted EBITDA of $284 million — a 45% year-over-year increase — for the quarter ended September 30. The retail casino operator, which also runs the ESPN Bet-branded interactive business, also swung back to profitability, posting net income of $32 million compared with an $865.1 million net loss in the third quarter of 2025.

Where the growth came from

PENN's retail segment delivered a record third-quarter revenue result, with the company citing "broad-based strength across the portfolio" and contributions from newly completed development projects. Gaming revenue across the business climbed to $1.37 billion from $1.32 billion a year earlier. Regionally, the Midwest segment posted the company's strongest year-over-year revenue growth at 14.4%, followed by 6% growth in the West, while the Northeast segment — which includes PENN's hotel-casino properties in Illinois, Pennsylvania, and Ohio — grew retail revenue 2.6% to $708.3 million and adjusted EBITDA to $208.1 million from $197.9 million.

The company's interactive segment, covering online sports betting, iGaming, and retail sportsbooks, generated $348.4 million in revenue, up from $297.7 million in the prior-year quarter, with online sports betting and iGaming growing 17% year over year combined. PENN also pointed to early momentum in Canada, where it said users and revenue per user grew in Ontario, its first Canadian market, and where it launched interactive products in Alberta — its second Canadian province — during the quarter.

What the company is saying

CEO Jay Snowden said the retail business "delivered better-than-expected revenue and Adjusted EBITDAR results, driven by same-store growth and contributions from our completed development projects," and that the company is "confident in achieving our full-year Adjusted EBITDA target" in its interactive segment. He added that the "healthy operating trends" across both retail and interactive operations "continued through October," pointing to momentum carrying into the current quarter. The company also noted that segment Adjusted EBITDAR margins improved year-over-year for the third consecutive quarter.
